daisy.context_note: Daisy is a broad image label, not a species identification. This reference is ONLY for Shasta daisy; confirm the plant type before applying it.

facts.sunlight: Shasta daisies grow in sunny positions and can also tolerate some shade.
facts.soil: Use soil enriched with organic material that drains freely. Poor drainage, especially in winter, is unsuitable.
facts.watering: Established Shasta daisies tolerate drought. The source does not provide a universal watering interval.
facts.pruning: Removing faded blooms encourages another flowering flush. Divide crowded clumps roughly every two to three years.

dandelion.context_note: This reference concerns common dandelion. The classifier does not establish botanical species.

facts.sunlight: Common dandelion grows in a sunny site; NC State lists at least six hours of direct sun.
facts.soil: Its long taproot allows it to establish in compacted ground.
facts.seasonal: It is a perennial that spreads readily through wind-carried seeds. It can contribute early-season food for pollinating insects.

rose.context_note: Rose varieties have different needs, especially for pruning. Confirm the variety; the image classifier has low rose recall.

facts.sunlight: A sunny location is generally preferred, although some roses tolerate lighter shade.
facts.soil: Choose fertile soil that holds moisture while allowing excess water to drain away.
facts.watering: Newly planted roses need regular watering while establishing. Established plants may need extra water in dry weather. Water the root area; container plants can dry faster than those in beds.
facts.pruning: Removing fading flowers can encourage further blooms. Pruning technique depends on the rose type; use its specific guide.

sunflower.context_note: This guide concerns common annual sunflower, not every perennial Helianthus species. Check the plant label and local climate.

facts.sunlight: Common annual sunflowers prefer a sunny, open position.
facts.soil: They prefer moist soil that drains well and can grow in loam, sand or clay.
facts.watering: Once established, common sunflowers can tolerate dry conditions. The source does not specify one fixed watering schedule.
facts.seasonal: This is a warm-season annual that does not tolerate frost. Taller cultivars may need staking and shelter from strong wind.

tulip.context_note: Tulip species and hybrids differ. The source describes temperate growing conditions; timing cannot be transferred directly to every climate.

facts.sunlight: Garden tulips generally grow best in a sunny position.
facts.soil: Use fertile soil with organic material and effective drainage. Persistent wetness can lead to bulb or root decay.
facts.watering: The source describes moderately moist growing soil and dry summer conditions, rather than a year-round fixed watering schedule.
facts.pruning: When retaining bulbs as perennials, remove spent flower stems but leave the leaves until they turn yellow.
facts.seasonal: Tulips suit cool, moist winters followed by warm, dry summers. Many hybrids flower less strongly in later years.
